In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Ghafir

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Forgiver of sin, and Accepter of repentance, severe in punishment, Possessor of abundance⦆. In this noble verse, may He who is Majestic and Exalted, has combined encouragement (al-targhib) and warning (al-tarhib), and promise (al-wa'd) and threat (al-wa'id); because the aspirations of intelligent people are confined to two matters: attracting benefit (jalb al-naf') and repelling harm (daf' al-durr). This meaning contained in this noble verse has come clarified in many verses of the Book of Allah,

• such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful. And that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [al-Hijr: 49-50].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "My punishment — I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me..."﴾ [al-A'raf: 156].

• And His saying, may He be exalted, at the end of al-An'am: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment﴾ ﴿and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-An'am: 165].

• And His saying in al-A'raf: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-A'raf: 167].

The verses of this kind are many and well known.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve﴾. In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that none dispute concerning the signs of Allah, meaning none contend about them, seeking to refute them and nullify what came in them, except the disbelievers.

Allah has made clear in another place the purpose that drives them to dispute about them, together with some of their attributes, in His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood in order to refute thereby the truth, and they have taken My signs and that which they are warned of as a mockery﴾ [al-Kahf: 56]. He clarified that purpose in this noble surah in His saying: ﴿And they disputed with falsehood in order to refute thereby the truth﴾ [Ghafir: 5].

We have already mentioned in Surat al-Hajj that among those who dispute concerning Allah are followers who follow their misguiding leaders, from the devils of mankind and jinn, and they are the ones mentioned in His saying: ﴿And among the people is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil﴾ ﴿It is decreed for him that whoever allies with him - indeed, he will misguide him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Hajj: 3-4].

And that among them are leaders, their followed chiefs, and they are the ones mentioned in His saying: ﴿And among the people is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book﴾ ﴿turning his side [in arrogance] to mislead from the way of Allah﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Hajj: 8-9].

And Allah has made clear in another place that among the kinds of the disbelievers' disputation is their disputing with the believers who responded to Allah and believed in Him and His Messenger, in order to return them to disbelief after belief. He showed the falsehood of their argument and threatened them with His wrath upon them and His severe punishment, and that is in His saying: ﴿And those who argue concerning Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is baseless with their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment﴾ [ash-Shura: 16].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So let not their movement throughout the lands deceive you﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, majestic and exalted, forbade His Prophet ﷺ, so as to legislate for his nation, that the movement of those who disbelieve through the lands of Allah should deceive him, through trade, profits, well-being and abundance of provision, as Quraysh had abundant wealth flowing to them from the profits of trade and other things, from the journey of winter and summer mentioned in His saying: ﴿The caravans of winter and summer﴾ [Quraysh: 2], that is, to Yemen and Syria, and they were, despite that, disbelievers and wrongdoers who denied the Prophet of Allah and opposed him.

The meaning: Do not be deceived by Allah's bestowal of blessings upon them, their movement through His lands in ease and well-being; for Allah, majestic and exalted, gradually leads them on (yastadriju) by that bestowal, granting them enjoyment of it for a little while, then He destroys them and makes their destination the Fire.

He has clarified this meaning in verses of His Book:

• Like His saying: ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the land deceive you. A brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Al 'Imran: 196-197].

• And His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves - let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts﴾ ﴿We will grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a massive punishment﴾ [Luqman: 23-24].

• And His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾ [al-Baqarah: 126].

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will not succeed. [Theirs is] enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus: 69-70].

And other verses besides these.

The fa' in His saying "fa-la yaghurrannaka" (so let not ... deceive you) is causative (sababiyyah), meaning: their movement in the lands of Allah, enjoying wealth and provision, should not be a cause for your being deceived by them, so that you think well of them; because that enjoyment is an enjoyment of gradual leading-on (istidraj), which is soon to vanish, and they are headed toward destruction and everlasting punishment.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus has the word of your Lord been justified against those who disbelieve, that they are companions of the Fire﴾. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read this letter (kalimat, "words") in the feminine sound plural form, while the rest read (kalimatu Rabbika, "the word of your Lord") in the singular.

We have already explained the meaning of al-kalimah (the word) and al-kalimat (the words) in a passage similar to this verse in surah Ya-Sin, in our discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly the word has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe﴾ [Ya-Sin: 7].

(p-382) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Ghafir

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And they seek forgiveness for those who believe﴾.

This noble verse indicates that the angels' seeking forgiveness for the people of the earth is specific to the believers among them. Another verse has come whose apparent meaning differs from this, namely His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And they seek forgiveness for whoever is on the earth﴾ [al-Shura: 5], to the end of the verse.

The answer is that the verse of Ghafir specifies (mukhassisa, i.e., restricts a general term by a specific one, takhsis) the verse of al-Shura, and the meaning is: "and they seek forgiveness for whoever is on the earth from among the believers," because of the obligation to restrict the general (al-'amm) by the specific (al-khass).

﴿And if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you﴾.

What comes to mind in this verse of the contradiction between the condition and the consequence concerning "some" is not hidden, because what suits the conditioning of truthfulness is that all of what he promises them befall them, not some of it. Yet He, exalted is He, did not say: "And if he is truthful, all of what he promises you will befall you." Answers have been given to this, and among the closest of them in my view is: the intended "some" that befalls them is the immediate "some," which is the punishment of this world, because they are more fearful of the immediate punishment, and because they are closer to believing in the punishment of this world than in the punishment of the Hereafter.

Another answer is that the meaning is: "If he is truthful, then at least some of what he promises you will befall you." On this basis, the point is exaggeration in warning, because when he warns them of the befalling of some, this conveys that it is destructive and frightening; so what of the whole? In it there is also a demonstration of complete fairness and the absence of partisanship. For this reason he placed first the possibility that he is lying.

Another answer is that the word "some" (ba'd) is used to mean "all" (kull). On this basis, the meaning of ﴿some of what he promises you﴾ is: "all of what he promises you." Among the evidences for this in the Arabic language is the saying of the poet:

Indeed, affairs, when the calamities manage them without the elders, you see a flaw in some of them.

That is, you see a flaw in them.

And the saying of al-Qutami:

The patient one may attain some of his need, and the hasty one may sometimes meet with a slip.

That is, the patient one may attain his need.

As for Abu 'Ubayda's use of this as evidence, with the saying of Labid:

Abandoner of places when I do not like them, or whose soul-seizing death seizes some of the souls,

it is an error on his part, because Labid's intended "some of the souls" is his own soul, as I have explained in my journey (ri79lati) in discussing His statement: ﴿And if a Qur'an were by it the mountains set in motion﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Ra'd: 31].

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which You promised them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring.﴾

He did not clarify here the verse that includes His promise of the Gardens to them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses and offspring.

However, He, exalted is He, made His promise to them in this way clear in Surat al-Ra'd, in His saying: ﴿Those who patiently seek the countenance of their Lord, establish the prayer, spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, and repel evil with good, for them is the final abode.﴾ ﴿Gardens of Eden, they will enter them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses and offspring, and the angels will enter upon them from every gate.﴾ [al-Hajj: 23 - 13]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will say: Our Lord, You made us die twice and gave us life twice.﴾ The verified position, from which one should not depart, is that the two deaths in this noble verse are: the first death, which is their state in their mothers' wombs as nutfah (a drop of fluid), 'alaqah (a clinging clot) and mudghah (a lump of flesh), before the soul is breathed into them. Before the soul is breathed into them, they have no life, so they are called dead in that respect.

The second death is their dying and their going to their graves when their terms in the life of this world come to an end.

The two lives are: the first life in the life of this world, and the second life, which is their resurrection from the graves for reckoning, recompense, and eternal abiding with no death in it, either in Paradise or in the Fire.

(p-375) The Qur'anic evidence that this is the verified interpretation of the verse is that Allah stated it plainly in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then give you life again, and then to Him you will be returned.﴾ (al-Baqarah: 28). By this you know that the other opinions regarding the verse have no reliable basis.

In my view, the more apparent justification that permits applying the name of death to the 'alaqah and mudghah, for example, in the wombs of mothers, is that the same thing, which is the very 'alaqah and mudghah, has stages (atwar), as Allah said: ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾ (Nuh: 14), and ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾ (al-Zumar: 6). Since that same thing has life in some of these stages and no life in others, it is correct to apply death and life to it as one thing, from which life is lifted at one time and present in it at another. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned a different justification for this, so consult him if you wish.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So we have acknowledged our sins; is there any way out?﴾ Allah, exalted is He, has made clear in other places that acknowledging sin at that time does not benefit, as He said: ﴿So they will acknowledge their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze﴾ (al-Mulk: 11). And He said: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us; we will act righteously; indeed we are certain﴾ (al-Sajdah: 12), and other verses besides these.

As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿Is there any way out?﴾, we have already explained it with Qur'anic verses in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: The messengers of our Lord had come with the truth. Are there any intercessors for us, that they may intercede for us, or are we to be returned so that we may act differently from what we used to do?﴾ (al-A'raf: 53).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because, when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved, but when partners were associated with Him, you believed.﴾ The discussion of this has already passed in Surat as-Saffat, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals. Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," would be arrogant﴾ [as-Saffat: 34-35], and so on.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Greatest.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Kahf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He does not share His judgment with anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 26].

(p-376) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs﴾. In this noble verse, He, glorified and exalted, mentions that He is the One who shows His creation His signs, meaning the cosmic, decreed signs (al-ayat al-kawniyyah al-qadariyyah), so that they may serve as indications to them of His lordship and of His right to be worshipped alone. Among those signs are the night, the day, the sun and the moon, as He said: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon﴾ [Fussilat: 37]. 

Among them are the heavens and the earths, and what is in them, the stars, the winds and the clouds, the seas and the rivers, the springs, the mountains, the trees, and the traces of peoples who were destroyed. As He said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day [...] are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164]. He also said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding﴾. He said: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾, ﴿And in your own creation and what He disperses of living creatures are signs for a people who are certain﴾, ﴿and the alternation of the night and the day, and what Allah sends down from the sky of provision, and with it revives the earth after its death, and the turning of the winds are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 3-5]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, are signs for a people who fear Him﴾ [Yunus: 6].

What He, glorified and exalted, mentioned in this verse of the believer (the Surah of al-Mu'min), that He is the One who shows His creation His signs, He explained and clarified further in other places. He made clear that He shows them His signs in the horizons and within themselves, and that His purpose in this manifestation is that it become clear to them that what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought is the truth, as He said: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

Al-afaq is the plural of ufq, which is the direction (or region). Allah, glorified and exalted, has made clear, from the wonders of His artistry and His marvels in the regions of His heavens and His earth, what makes it clear to every person of reason that He is the Lord, worshipped alone. As we have pointed out, [these include] the sun, the moon, the stars, the trees, the mountains, the animals and the seas, and other things besides.

He also made clear that among His signs, which He shows them and which it is not possible for them to deny in any part, is His subjecting the cattle to them, so that they may ride them, eat of their flesh, benefit from their milk, its butter, its ghee and its aqit (dried curd), and wear their hides, wool, fleece and hair. As He said: ﴿Allah is He who made for you the cattle, that you may ride some of them and eat from them﴾ ﴿And for you in them are benefits, and that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts, and upon them and upon the ships you are carried﴾ ﴿And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah will you deny?﴾ [Ghafir: 79-81].

(p-377) He also made clear in some places that among His signs, which He shows to some of His creation, are the miracles of His messengers, because miracles are signs, meaning indications and marks of the truthfulness of the messengers. As He said concerning Pharaoh: ﴿And We had certainly shown him all Our signs, but he denied and refused﴾ [Ta-Ha: 56]. And He made clear in another place that among His signs, which He shows His creation, is His punishment of those who deny His messengers, as He said in the story of His destruction of the people of Lut: ﴿And We have left of it a clear sign for a people who reason﴾ [al-Ankabut: 35].

And He said concerning His punishment of Pharaoh and his people with the flood, the locusts, the lice, etc.: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts and the lice and the frogs and the blood, as distinct signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 133].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He sends down for you provision from the sky﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, glorified and exalted, used the word provision (rizq) and meant rain, because rain is the cause of provision. Using the effect (al-musabbab) to mean its cause (sababuh), because of the close connection between them, is a well-known Arabic idiom. Likewise its reverse, which is using the cause to mean the effect, as in the line of poetry:

"I have eaten blood, if I do not make you [wife] a co-wife, far from the place of the earring's fall, fragrant of scent."

Here he used "blood" and meant the blood-money (diyah), because it is its cause.

In our treatise titled Man' Jawaz al-Majaz fi al-Manzil lil-Ta'abbud wal-I'jaz (Prohibiting the Permissibility of Metaphor in the Revealed Text, for Worship and Inimitability), we have explained that such expressions are Arabic idioms, which the Arabs spoke in their language and in which the Qur'an was revealed. What the scholars of rhetoric (ulama al-balaghah) say, that the verse contains what they call the metonymic figure (al-majaz al-mursal), whose relations they count as causal and effect-based, has no need for it and no proof for it, and must be referred back [to the plain sense].

The use of the word provision in this verse of the believer for rain has a parallel in another place, such as His saying at the beginning of Surat al-Jathiyah: ﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky of provision, and with it revives the earth after its death﴾ [verse 5]. By His saying "and with it revives the earth after its death" He made clear that His intended meaning by provision is rain, because rain is what Allah uses to revive the earth after its death.

Allah, glorified and exalted, also made clear that rain is called provision only because rain is the cause of provision in many verses of His Book, as in His saying in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And He sent down from the sky water, and with it brought forth fruits as provision for you﴾ [verse 22]. The preposition "bi" (with) in His saying "with it brought forth" indicates causation, as you see.

(p-378) And as in His saying in Surat Ibrahim: ﴿Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth and sent down from the sky water, and with it brought forth fruits as provision for you, and subjected to you the ships﴾ [verse 32]. And His saying in Surat Qaf: ﴿And We sent down from the sky blessed water, and with it caused to grow gardens and grain of harvest﴾ ﴿and tall date palms with ordered spathes﴾ ﴿as provision for the servants﴾ [Qaf: 9-11].

He also made clear in other verses that the provision mentioned includes what people eat and what cattle eat, because what cattle eat results in people benefiting from their flesh, hides, milk, wool, fleece and hair, as already mentioned. As in His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which eat their livestock and themselves? Will they not then see?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 27]. And His saying: ﴿It is He who sent down from the sky water, for you from it is drink, and from it is [vegetation] in which you pasture [your livestock]﴾ ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, the olives, the palm trees, the grapes, and from all the fruits﴾ [al-Nahl: 10-11].

His saying "in which you pasture" (fihi tusimun) means that you leave your livestock to graze in it, eating from it without having to bear the burden of fodder for them, as has already been explained with its Arabic evidence in Surat al-Nahl. And as in His saying: ﴿And He sent down from the sky water, and We brought forth thereby pairs of various plants. Eat and let your livestock graze﴾ [Ta-Ha: 53-54]. And His saying: ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firm, as enjoyment for you and for your livestock﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 31-33], and other verses besides.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And none will be mindful except one who turns back in repentance﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned that none of the people is mindful of these signs, meaning that none is admonished by these signs referred to in His saying: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky. And none will be mindful except one who turns back [to Allah]﴾, meaning one whom Allah has granted the inclination to turn back to Him.

Inabah (turning back in repentance) is returning from disbelief and sins to faith and obedience.

These who turn back, who are mindful, who are admonished, are the people of sound minds, free from the flaws of impairment, who are mentioned in His saying at the beginning of Surat Al 'Imran: ﴿And none will be mindful except those of understanding﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7], and in His saying in Surat Ibrahim: ﴿That they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may be mindful﴾ [Ibrahim: 52], (p-379) and other verses besides.

This verse of the believer, and what is in its meaning of verses, indicates that other than those of understanding, the mindful ones mentioned just above, do not take heed and are not admonished by the signs, but rather turn away from them with the utmost aversion.

This meaning has been made clear in many verses of the Book of Allah:

• As in His saying: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it?﴾ [Yusuf: 105].

• And His saying: ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "Continuous magic."﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]

• And His saying: ﴿And when they see a sign, they mock﴾ [al-Saffat: 14].

And His saying: ﴿Say, "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth. But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101], and His saying: ﴿And no sign comes to them from among the signs of their Lord but that they turn away from it﴾ [Ya-Sin: 46], in al-An'am and Ya-Sin, and other verses besides.

Allah's saying: ﴿So call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾. We have already presented the discussion of verses like this one at the beginning of Surah az-Zumar, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿So worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion. Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion﴾ [az-Zumar: 2-3].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He sends down the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants, that he may warn of the Day of Meeting﴾ ﴿the Day when they will come forth, nothing of them concealed from Allah﴾. We have already given its clarification with Qur'anic verses at the beginning of Surat an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants, [saying], "Warn that there is no deity except Me, so fear Me."﴾ [an-Nahl: 2].

• And His saying, exalted is He, in this verse of the believer: ﴿The Day they will come forth; nothing of them will be concealed from Allah﴾, similar to it has come in many verses,

• such as His saying about their emergence on that Day: ﴿On the Day the earth will be replaced by other than the earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ibrahim: 48].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will all come forth before Allah, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers..."﴾ the verse [Ibrahim: 21].

And

• such as His saying about their state that nothing of them is concealed from Allah on that Day: ﴿On that Day you will be presented, and nothing of you will be concealed﴾ [al-Haqqah: 18].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is ever Aware of them﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 11].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, nothing on earth or in the heaven is concealed from Allah﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 5]. The verses similar to this are many, and we have explained them at the beginning of Surat Hud, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their chests to hide from Him﴾ the verse [Hud: 5], and we mentioned a portion of that at the beginning of Surat Saba', in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Knower of the unseen; not an atom's weight escapes Him in the heavens or on the earth﴾ the verse [Saba': 3]. (p-380)

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And warn them of the Day of the Imminent, when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief.﴾ Al-indhar (warning), and information accompanied specifically by a threat. Every warning is an information, but not every information is a warning.

We have already clarified the meaning of indhar (warning) and its types at the beginning of Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿A Book revealed to you, so let there be no constriction in your breast about it, that you may warn thereby﴾ and the verse [al-A'raf: 2].

The apparent meaning is that His saying here, "the Day of the Imminent," is the second object of indhar (warning), not an adverbial of time, because warning and intimidation about the Day of Resurrection take place in the life of this world. Al-Azifah means the Resurrection. That is: warn them of the Day of Resurrection, meaning frighten them with it and threaten them with its great terrors, so that they may prepare for it in this world through faith and obedience.

The Resurrection was referred to as al-Azifah because of its uzuf, that is, its nearness. The Arabs say: azifa al-tarahhul (the departure drew near), with the zay vowelled with a kasra, ya'zafu with a fatha on it, azafan with two fathas according to the regular pattern, and uzufan. So he is a'zif, against the regular pattern, in the last verbal noun. The adjective means that its time has drawn near and its occurrence has become imminent. From this is the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani:

Azifa al-tarahhul (the departure has drawn near), but our mounts have not yet moved from our saddles, as if it had already come.

It is also narrated as afida al-tarahhul, and the meaning of both is one.

The meaning: ﴿And warn them of the Day of the Imminent﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, whose coming and occurrence are near.

What this noble verse includes of the nearness of the Hour has been clarified in other verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿The Imminent has drawn near; none besides Allah can disclose it﴾ [al-Najm: 57-58],

• His saying: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ and the verse [al-Qamar: 1],

• His saying: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near for them﴾ and the verse [al-Anbiya': 1].

• His saying in al-Ahzab: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Ahzab: 63].

• His saying in al-Shura: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Shura: 17].

(p-381)

We have already presented this at the beginning of Surat al-Nahl in the discussion of His saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Nahl: 1].

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief﴾. The apparent reading is that idh is an apposition to yawm, and on this basis it is of the category of the object, not the adverbial of time, as we explained a moment ago.

Al-qulub: plural of qalb (heart), which is well known.

Ladá: an adverb meaning "at" or "near" (ʿinda).

Al-hanajir: plural of hanjara (throat), which is well known.

Regarding the meaning of hearts being at the throats at that time, the scholars of tafsir have two well-known views:

The first: what Qatada and others said, that their hearts on that Day will rise from their places in the chests until they cling to the throats, so they are at the throats; neither do they come out of their mouths so that they die, nor do they return to their places in the chests so that they breathe. This view is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

The second view: the intended meaning of hearts being at the throats is to express the intensity of the terror and the awfulness of the matter. On this basis the verse is like His saying: ﴿And when the eyes swerved and the hearts reached the throats, and you thought about Allah with various thoughts. There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10-11], and it is a shaking of fear and dread, not a shaking of the movement of the earth.

His saying in this noble verse: kazimin (choking) means distressed, filled with fear, grief and sorrow.

Al-kazm: the recurring of fear, anger and sorrow in the heart until it fills with it and is constricted by it.

The Arabs say: kazamtu al-siqa (I filled the waterskin) when I filled it with water and tied it tight.

The saying of some that kazimin means silent does not contradict what we have mentioned, because the fear and grief that fill their hearts prevent them from speech, so they are unable to speak. From the use of kazm for silence is the verse of al-Ajjaj:

And many a company of pilgrims, silenced from idle talk and obscene speech.

The meaning of the saying of one who said kazimin means: they do not speak except one whom Allah permits and who says what is right, also returns to this view, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿They will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is right﴾ [al-Naba': 38].

His saying kazimin is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the people whose hearts these are, in meaning. The implied sense: when their hearts are at their throats, while they are choking, that is, filled with fear, grief and sorrow. It is not far-fetched that it is a circumstantial clause from the hearts themselves, since they are described with kazm, which is a description of their owners.

A parallel in the Qur'an is: ﴿Indeed, I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me﴾ [Yusuf: 4], where in this noble verse He applied to the stars, sun and moon the attribute of rational beings in His saying "I saw them prostrating," and what justifies it is that He described the stars, sun and moon with prostration, which is an attribute of rational beings.

A similar parallel is His saying: ﴿If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the sky, and their necks would remain humbly bowed to it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 4], and His saying: ﴿They said, "We come willingly"﴾ [Fussilat: 11].

His saying: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend nor an intercessor who is obeyed﴾. We have already presented the discussion of this in Surat al-Baqara and Surat al-A'raf, and we have referred to it repeatedly.

Allah's saying: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.﴾ We have already presented the discussion of the verses similar to this one at the beginning of Surat Hud and elsewhere, and we have also referred to it repeatedly.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾ ﴿to Pharaoh and Haman and Qarun, but they said, "A sorcerer, a liar."﴾ In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that He sent His prophet Moses, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace, with His signs and his clear proofs, such as the staff and the white hand, to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun (p-383), but they denied him and claimed that he was a sorcerer.

He clarified this meaning in many verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He, about Pharaoh and his people: ﴿And they said, "Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with it, we will not believe you"﴾ [al-A'raf: 132].

• His saying, exalted is He, about Pharaoh: ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71].

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said to the eminent around him, "Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 34].

The verses with similar meaning are many. We have explained them in several places in this blessed Book.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Moses said, "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, mentions that His prophet Moses, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, sought refuge in his Lord, i.e., he sought protection in Him and safeguarded himself, from every arrogant one, i.e., one characterized by arrogance, who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning, i.e., does not affirm the resurrection and the recompense.

The reason for Moses' seeking refuge in his Lord mentioned here is that Pharaoh said to his people: ﴿"Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land."﴾ [Ghafir: 26].

So Moses' seeking refuge in Allah mentioned here is in reality from Pharaoh, although the expression is more general than Pharaoh specifically, because Pharaoh is undoubtedly arrogant and does not believe in the Day of Reckoning, so he is included in the statement in the first instance, and he is the intended meaning of the statement.

What Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse of the Believer, of Moses' seeking refuge in Allah from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning, such as Pharaoh and the obstinate leaders of his people, He mentioned something similar in Surah ad-Dukhan in His saying, exalted is He, about Moses addressing Pharaoh and his people: ﴿"And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me."﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 20], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 28:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And a man of the family of Pharaoh, a believer, who was concealing his faith, said: "Would you kill a man for saying, 'My Lord is God'?"﴾

In this noble verse, the Exalted has mentioned that a believing man from the family of Pharaoh was concealing his faith, meaning he was hiding from them that he was a believer. He denounced Pharaoh and his people for their intention to kill the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him (p-384) and upon our Prophet, when Pharaoh said: ﴿Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord﴾ [Ghafir: 26], and so on. Yet he (Moses) had committed no offence that would warrant killing, except that he said, "My Lord is God."

In other verses, He has explained that it is customary for the polytheists to kill the Muslims, to torment them, and to expel them from their homes without any wrongdoing on their part, except that they believe in God and say, "Our Lord is God."

Such as His statement, exalted is He, concerning the People of the Trench, who burned the believers: ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench, the fire full of fuel, when they sat over it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. And they resented them only because they believed in God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Buruj: 4–8].

And His statement: ﴿Permission is given to those who are being fought because they have been wronged, and indeed God is able to give them victory. [They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right, only because they say, "Our Lord is God."﴾ [al-Hajj: 39–40].

And His statement concerning those who were sorcerers for Pharaoh and became among the best of the believers, when Pharaoh threatened them, saying: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, then I will crucify you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 124], that they replied to him with what God related of them in His statement: ﴿They said, "Indeed, to our Lord we will return. And you do not resent us except because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us."﴾ [al-A'raf: 125–126].

And other verses besides these.

The verified view is that the believing man mentioned in this verse was from the group of Pharaoh's people, as is apparent from His statement: ﴿from the family of Pharaoh﴾.

As for the claim that he was an Israelite and that there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the speech, and that "from the family of Pharaoh" is connected to "concealing" (yaktumu), meaning "a believing man said, concealing his faith from the family of Pharaoh," i.e., hiding his faith from Pharaoh and his people, it contradicts the verified view, as is not hidden.

It has been said that this believing man is the one who said to Moses: ﴿Indeed, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you, so leave﴾ [al-Qasas: 20]. It has also been said that it was someone else.

The scholars differed greatly regarding his name. It was said: his name is Habib; it was said: his name is Sham'an; it was said: his name is Hizqil; and other things were said, but there is no evidence for any of these.

The apparent view regarding the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of the verbal noun formed by "an" and its following clause in His statement in this noble verse, ﴿an yaqula Rabbiya Allah﴾ ("that he says, My Lord is God"), is that it is a maf'ul li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

(p-385) Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said in his Sahih, in the tafsir of this noble verse: "'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir told me, who said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi told me, 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr told me, who said: I said to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: Tell me about the worst thing the polytheists did to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He said: 'While the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was praying in the courtyard of the Ka'bah, 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt came, seized the shoulder of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), twisted his garment around his neck, and choked him with a severe choking. Then Abu Bakr came, seized his shoulder, pushed him away from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and said: "Would you kill a man for saying, 'My Lord is God'? He has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord."'"

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 40, verse 29:**

Allah says: ﴿Pharaoh said, "I only show you what I see, and I only guide you to the path of right conduct."﴾ The apparent meaning is that *araa* (see/perceive) in this noble verse is *'ilmiyyah 'irfaniyyah* (cognitive, in the sense of knowing through recognition), and it takes one object, as he indicated in the *Khulasah* (the versified summary of Arabic grammar by Ibn Malik) with his statement:

*For knowledge of recognition and for suspicion (tuhmah), transitivity to one object is obligatory.*

According to this, the meaning is: Pharaoh said, "I only inform you and make you aware of the truth about Moses, and that he should be killed, for fear that he will change your religion and spread corruption in your land," ﴿except what I see﴾, i.e., "I know and recognize that it is the truth and the correct position, so I do not hide from you anything contrary to what I display to you." ﴿And I only guide you to this, except to the path of right conduct﴾, i.e., the way of soundness and correctness.

These two matters that Allah mentions Pharaoh said in this noble verse have been shown in other verses to be lies on Pharaoh's part, each one of them.

As for the first, which is his saying ﴿I only show you what I see﴾, Allah has made clear his lying in it in verses of His Book, and He explained in them that he knows and is certain that the signs which Moses brought are true, and that none sent them down except Allah, and that he denied them, he and those among his people who were certain of them, in order to deceive the ignorant among them, as in His saying in Surat al-Naml: ﴿And insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease, among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ ﴿But when Our signs came to them as clear evidence, they said, "This is obvious magic."﴾ ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. So see how was the end of the corrupters.﴾ [An-Naml: 12–14].

(p. 386) So His saying in this verse: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾ is clear evidence that Pharaoh was lying in his saying: "I only show you what I see."

And like His saying in Surat Bani Isra'il: ﴿He said, "You have certainly known that none has sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidences. And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed."﴾ [Al-Isra': 102]. So the saying of Allah's Prophet Moses to Pharaoh, ﴿You have certainly known that none has sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾, emphasizing with an oath his statement that Pharaoh knows this, also indicates that he was lying in his saying: "I only show you what I see."

Pharaoh's purpose in this lie was deception and delusion, so that the ignorant among his people would think that he had the truth, as Allah indicated in His saying: ﴿So he deceived his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 54].

As for the second matter, which is his saying ﴿And I only guide you to the path of right conduct﴾, Allah has made clear his lying in it in verses of His Book, such as His saying: ﴿So they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not rightly guided.﴾ [Hud: 97]. And His saying: ﴿And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 79].

Some scholars said regarding His saying ﴿I only show you what I see﴾: meaning, "I only advise you with what I see for myself, of killing Moses." And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 40:

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like﴾. This noble verse and others like it, which indicate that evil deeds are not multiplied and are not recompensed except with their like, have been explained alongside other verses which indicate that evil deeds may sometimes be multiplied in certain circumstances, such as the saying of Allah, the Exalted, regarding our Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾ [al-Isra: 75], and His saying, the Exalted, regarding his wives, may Allah be pleased with them: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold﴾ [33]. This is a well-known difficulty (ishkal).

We have already presented its answer clearly in surah al-Naml, in the discussion of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be thrown into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ [al-Naml: 90].

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise, being provided therein without account﴾ (p-387). We have already clarified the meaning of this noble verse, explained righteous deed by means of Qur'anic verses, and clarified the verses that explain the principle of contrary implication (mafhum al-mukhalafa) in the saying: ﴿while being a believer﴾, in several places of this blessed book: in surah al-Nahl, in the discussion of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ and the verse [al-Nahl: 97]; and at the beginning of surah al-Kahf, in the discussion of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿and give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward, remaining therein forever﴾ [al-Kahf: 2-3].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 41:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And you invite me to the Fire﴾ ﴿You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge﴾. The apparent meaning is that the clause "you invite me" ﴿you invite me to disbelieve﴾ is a substitute (badal) for His saying ﴿And you invite me to the Fire﴾, because the call to disbelief in Allah and to associating partners with Him is a call to the Fire.

What this noble verse includes, namely that disbelief and associating partners with Allah necessitate entry into the Fire, Allah the Exalted has made clear in many verses of His Book, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 72]. We have already presented what suffices regarding this in surah al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah is as if he had fallen from the sky﴾ [al-Hajj: 31], and so on.

The true and undoubted position is that this speech is from the believer of Pharaoh's family whom God mentioned, and Moses had no part in it.

As for His saying, ﴿So you will remember what I say to you﴾, it means that on the Day of Resurrection they will know the truth of what he used to tell them, and will recall his advice, and so they will regret, though regret will not benefit them. The verses that indicate the like of this, that the disbelievers will have the realities of what they used to deny in this world revealed to them on the Day of Resurrection, are numerous, such as:

- His saying, ﴿And your people denied it, though it is the truth. Say: I am not a guardian over you. For every news there is a fixed time, and you will come to know﴾ [al-An'am: 66–67].
- His saying, ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [Sad: 88].
- His saying, ﴿No! They will soon know. Again, no! They will soon know﴾ [an-Naba': 4–5].
- His saying, ﴿No! You will soon know. Again, no! You will soon know﴾ [at-Takathur: 3–4].
- His saying, ﴿So We removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp﴾ [Qaf: 22].

along with other verses besides these.

As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿And I entrust my affair to God; indeed God is Seeing of the servants﴾ [Ghafir: 44], and ﴿So God protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾ [Ghafir: 45], this is clear evidence that true reliance upon God, and entrusting one's affairs to Him, is a cause of protection and safeguarding from every evil. It has been established in the foundational works (al-Usul, the principles of legal theory and Arabic grammar) that the fa' (ف) is among the particles of causation (huruf al-ta'lil), as in the saying of people: ﴿sahā fa-sajada﴾ (sahā fa-sajada), meaning he prostrated because of his forgetfulness; and ﴿saraqa fa-qutiʿat yaduhu﴾ (saraqa fa-qutiʿat yaduhu), meaning his hand was cut because of his theft, as we have mentioned repeatedly.

What this noble verse includes, namely that reliance upon God is a cause of safeguarding and protection from evil, is made clear in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon God, He is sufficient for him﴾ [at-Talaq: 3]. And His saying: ﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it increased them in faith, and they said, "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." So they returned with a blessing from God and bounty, no harm touched them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 173–174].

We have mentioned the verses indicating this at length at the beginning of Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Do not take other than Me as a guardian﴾ [al-Isra': 2].

It is apparent that the mā (ما) in His saying ﴿the evils of what they plotted﴾ [Ghafir: 45] is a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyyah), meaning: God protected him from the evils of their plotting, that is, the harms of their plotting and its hardships. The makr (مكر) is kayd (scheming).

This noble verse indicates that Pharaoh and his people intended to scheme against this noble believer, and that God protected him, that is, preserved and saved him, from the harms of their plotting and its hardships, because of his reliance upon God and his entrusting his affair to Him.

Some scholars say: God saved him from them along with Moses and his people. Others say: he climbed a mountain, and God made them unable to reach him and saved him from them. All of this has no evidence for it. What the Qur'an clearly indicates is only that God protected him from the evils of their plotting, that is, preserved him and saved him from them.

As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿And the evil torment encompassed the family of Pharaoh﴾, its meaning is: when they intended to scheme against this believer, God protected him from their scheme and turned the evil outcome back upon them. So He returned the evil of their plotting upon them. Thus the aforementioned believer was saved in this world and the Hereafter, while Pharaoh and his people were destroyed in this world, the Hereafter, and the barzakh (the intermediate state).

Regarding their destruction in this world He said: ﴿And We drowned the family of Pharaoh﴾, and similar verses.

Regarding their state in the barzakh He said: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir: 46].

Regarding their punishment in the Hereafter He said: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the family of Pharaoh to the severest torment"﴾ [Ghafir: 46].

As for what this noble verse indicates of the encompassing of evil scheming upon its schemer, God clarified it in His saying: ﴿And evil scheming does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].

The Arabs say: ḥāqa bihi al-makrūh (حاق به المكروه) yaḥīqu bihi ḥayqan wa-ḥuyūqan (يحيق به حيقا وحيوقا), when the disliked thing descended upon him and surrounded him. It is not used except for the encompassing of something disliked specifically. One says: ḥāqa bihi al-sūʾ wa-al-makrūh (حاق به السوء والمكروه), but one does not say: ḥāqa bihi al-khayr (حاق به الخير). The root ḥ-y-q is from the hollow verb (al-ajwaf) whose middle radical is yā' (ي), and its active participle is ḥā'iq (حائق) by analogy. From it is the saying of the poet:

"He trampled the swift horses upon the stronghold of their homes, and the power of Dabba encompassed them, the encompassing one."

We have already stated that the morphological pattern of sayyi'ah (سيئة) on the morphological scale is fay'alah (فيعلة), derived from al-sū' (السوء). The yā' of the added fay'alah was assimilated into the wāw which is the root consonant of the word, after the wāw was changed into yā' according to the morphological rule referred to, in the Khulasa (the versified summary of Arabic morphology) in the verse:

"If the preceding letter, from a wāw and a yā', is quiescent, and they are joined, and it is not from a metrical deficiency, then the yā' of the wāw is made to be assimilated (lin muday-ghaman). And the one who gives (muʿṭī, مُعطي) is anomalous, contrary to what is written."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 47:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when they argue with one another in the Fire, and the weak say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were to you followers, so will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?"﴾ ﴿Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between [His] servants."﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿yataḥājjūna fī al-nār﴾ [they argue with one another in the Fire]. Its root is yatafā'alūna, from al-ḥujjah (proof, argument), meaning: they dispute with one another, and each seeks to prove his case against the other. What this noble verse includes is clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah:

• Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, that is the truth: the dispute of the people of the Fire﴾ [Ṣād: 64].

• And His saying, exalted is He: (p-390) ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning word to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers." Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals." And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, [it was] the planning by night and day when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him."﴾ [Saba': 31–33].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister [nation], until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know." And the first of them will say to the last of them, "You had no virtue over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."﴾ [al-A'rāf: 38–39].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their ties are cut off from them. And those who followed will say, "If only we had another return, we would disassociate ourselves from them as they have disassociated themselves from us."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166–167].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will come forth to Allah all together, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were to you followers, so can you relieve us of anything of the punishment of Allah?" They will say, "If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we show anguish or are patient; there is for us no place of escape."﴾ ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had over you no authority, except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in your association of me [with Allah] before."﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 21–22].

Verses similar to these are many, and we have already discussed them at several points in this blessed book.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 49:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."﴾ In this noble verse, may He be exalted, He mentions that the people of the Fire asked the keepers of Hell to call upon Allah on their behalf, that He might lighten for them some of the severity of the punishment of the Fire.

In Surat az-Zukhruf, He has made clear that they called out to Malik specifically, from among the keepers of the people of the Fire, that Allah would decree upon them, meaning that He would cause them to die, so that they might find rest in death from the punishment of the Fire.

Moreover, may He be exalted, has made clear in verses of His Book that they will not be granted favour in either of the two matters: the punishment they asked to have lightened in this Surat al-Mu'min will not be lightened for them, and the death they asked for in Surat az-Zukhruf will not come to them. Concerning the non-lightening of the punishment for them, He, may He be exalted, said in this verse (p-391): ﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?" They will say, "Yes." They will say, "Then call upon them yourselves." But the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾ [Ghafir: 50]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful disbeliever﴾ [Fatir: 36]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So We will not increase you except in punishment﴾ [78]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Their punishment will not be relaxed for them, and they therein will be in despair﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 75]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, its punishment was ever a continuing torment﴾ [al-Furqan: 65]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So it will be an inseparable punishment﴾ [al-Furqan: 77]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Their punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved﴾ [Al 'Imran: 88]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And for them is an enduring punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 37].

He, may He be exalted, said concerning their not dying in the Fire: ﴿It will not be decreed for them so that they would die﴾ [Fatir: 36]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Death will come to him from every place, but he will not die﴾ [Ibrahim: 17]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Every time their skins are fully cooked, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment﴾ [an-Nisa': 56]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live﴾ [Ta-Ha: 74]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And the most wretched will avoid it, who will enter the greatest Fire. Then he will neither die therein nor live﴾ [al-A'la: 11-13].

And when they said: ﴿Let your Lord decree upon us﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 77], He answered them with His saying: ﴿He said, "Indeed, you will remain"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 77].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say: "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?"﴾ We have already discussed this verse, together with the verses that have a similar meaning, in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15].

Al-Shinqiti's commentary (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand up﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Al 'Imran, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a prophet fought, with him, many devoted followers (ribbiyyun kathir)﴾ [Al 'Imran: 146], and we mentioned a portion of that in As-Saffat, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And certainly has Our word preceded for Our servants the messengers, that they would surely be helped, and indeed, Our soldiers will be the victorious﴾ [As-Saffat: 171-172]. And further clarification of it will come, God willing, in Surah Al-Mujadila.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى الهُدى وأوْرَثْنا بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ الكِتابَ هُدًى وذِكْرى لِأُولِي الألْبابِ﴾ . [p. 392] اللّامُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى الهُدى﴾ مُوطِئَةٌ لِلْقَسَمِ (the introductory *lam*, *lam al-muwaṭṭi'ah*, which prepares the way for an oath), وصِيغَةُ الجَمْعِ في آتَيْنا و أوْرَثْنا لِلتَّعْظِيمِ (and the plural form in *ātaynā* and *awrathnā* is for glorification).

والمُرادُ بِالهُدى ما تَضَمَّنَهُ التَّوْراةُ مِنَ الهُدى في العَقائِدِ والأعْمالِ (the guidance intended by *al-hudā* is what the Torah contained of guidance in beliefs and deeds): وأوْرَثْنا بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ الكِتابَ وهو التَّوَراةُ (and We made the Children of Israel inherit the Book, which is the Torah). وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿هُدًى وذِكْرى لِأُولِي الألْبابِ﴾ مَفْعُولٌ مِن أجْلِهِ (*hudan* is an object of purpose, *mafʿūl min ajlihi*, i.e., an accusative of purpose)، أيْ: لِأجْلِ الهُدى والتَّذْكِيرِ (meaning: for the sake of guidance and reminder).

وَقالَ بَعْضُهم: هُدًى حالٌ (some of them said: *hudan* is a circumstantial accusative, *ḥāl*)، ووُرُودُ المَصْدَرِ المُنْكَّرِ حالًا مَعْرُوفٌ (and the occurrence of an indefinite verbal noun (*maṣdar munakkar*) as a circumstantial accusative is well known)، كَما أشارَ لَهُ في الخُلاصَةِ بِقَوْلِهِ (as he indicated in *al-Khulāsah*, in his saying):

وَمَصْدَرٍ مُنَكَّرٍ حالًا يَقَعْ بِكَثْرَةٍ كَـ بَغْتَةً زِيدٌ طَلَعْ

(And an indefinite verbal noun comes frequently as a circumstantial accusative, like *baghtatan* in "Zayd came out suddenly.")

وَقالَ القُرْطُبِيُّ: هُدًى بَدَلٌ مِنَ الكِتابِ (*hudan* is an apposition/substitute, *badal*, for *al-Kitāb*)، أوْ خَبَرُ مُبْتَدَأٍ مَحْذُوفٍ (or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, *khabar mubtada' maḥdhūf*)، وما تَضَمَّنَتْهُ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ الكَرِيمَةُ مِن أنَّ اللَّهَ أنْزَلَ التَّوْراةَ عَلى مُوسى وأنْزَلَ فِيها الهُدى لِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ جاءَ مُوَضَّحًا في آياتٍ مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ (and what this noble verse contains, that God sent down the Torah to Moses and sent down in it guidance for the Children of Israel, has been made clear in verses of the Book of God),

• كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَآتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ وجَعَلْناهُ هُدًى لِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ ألّا تَتَّخِذُوا مِن دُونِي ‎وَكِيلًا﴾ [الإسراء: ٢] .

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ فَلا تَكُنْ في مِرْيَةٍ مِن لِقائِهِ وجَعَلْناهُ هُدًى لِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾ الآيَةَ [السجدة: ٢٣] .

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنّا أنْزَلْنا التَّوْراةَ فِيها هُدًى ونُورٌ يَحْكُمُ بِها النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أسْلَمُوا لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا والرَّبّانِيُّونَ والأحْبارُ﴾ [المائدة: ٤٤]

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ مِن بَعْدِ ما أهْلَكْنا القُرُونَ الأُولى بَصائِرَ لِلنّاسِ وهُدًى ورَحْمَةً لَعَلَّهم يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ [القصص: ٤٣]

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ تَمامًا عَلى الَّذِي أحْسَنَ وتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وهُدًى ورَحْمَةً لَعَلَّهم بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [الأنعام: ١٥٤] .

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَكَتَبْنا لَهُ في الألْواحِ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ الآيَةَ [الأعراف: ١٤٥] .

إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الآياتِ.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but greatness (kibr), which they will never attain﴾. We have already explained this in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "Then descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein"﴾ [al-A'raf: 13], and we mentioned there some of the evil consequences that arise from arrogance (kibr).

Allah's saying: ﴿Surely the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾.

We have already mentioned that this verse is among the proofs indicating the Resurrection (al-ba'th). We have also explained all the proofs indicating the Resurrection by means of the Qur'anic verses, in abundance, in Surat al-Baqarah and Surat al-Nahl, and we have referred to the places of that many times.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 58:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor those who believe and do righteous deeds, nor the evildoer﴾. His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: "And not equal are the blind and the seeing," we have already discussed its meaning in Surah Hud, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The likeness of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf and the seeing and the hearing﴾ [Hud: 24], and so on.

And His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Nor those who believe and do righteous deeds, nor the evildoer﴾. Or shall We make the righteous like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 59:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is surely coming; there is no doubt about it, but most of the people do not believe.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Furqan, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, they denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blaze﴾ [al-Furqan: 11].

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 60:

God's words: ﴿Your Lord says: Call upon Me, and I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled.﴾

Some scholars said: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you" means: worship Me, and I will reward you for your worship. What supports this is His words after it: "Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled."

Some other scholars said: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you" means: ask Me, and I will give to you.

There is no contradiction between the two views, because supplicating to God is one of the forms of worshipping Him.

We have already clarified this meaning and explained how to reconcile His words, ﴿When My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 186], with His words, ﴿He will remove that for which you call upon Him, if He wills﴾ (p-394). That explanation makes it unnecessary to repeat it here.

The Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah is the One who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day to see by. Indeed Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾ We have already presented its explanation with Qur'anic verses in Surah al-Furqan, in the discussion of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who made the night for you as a garment, and sleep as rest, and made the day a resurrection.﴾ [al-Furqan: 47], and in Surah al-Isra' in the discussion of His words, the Exalted: ﴿So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible, that you might seek bounty from your Lord.﴾ [al-Isra': 12].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 67:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then He brings you forth as a child, then [He lets you reach] your maturity, then [He lets you reach] old age, and among you is one who is taken in death before that, so that you may reach an appointed term, and perhaps you will understand.﴾ We have already explained its meaning with Qur'anic verses in Surah al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection, then indeed, We created you from dust, then from a drop of semen...﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], and in other places.

Al-Shinqiti's commentary on surah 40, verse 68:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. We have already clarified this with Qur'anic verses in surah al-Nahl, in the discussion of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [al-Nahl: 40]. And we explained the modes of recitation (wujuh al-qira'ah) of His words there: "fa-yakunu" (and it is).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 76:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein; and wretched is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ Here, exalted and most high is He, did not specify the number of the gates of Hell, but He did specify that in Surat al-Hijr, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all. It has seven gates; for each gate is a portion designated.﴾ [al-Hijr: 43-44].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 40, verse 78:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did send messengers before you; of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you.﴾ What this noble verse contains, that Allah, blessed and exalted is He, related to His Prophet ﷺ the accounts of some of the messengers, namely Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Shu'ayb and Moses, and that He did not relate to him the accounts of other messengers, is clarified elsewhere in this passage. Such is His saying in Surah an-Nisa': ﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you. And Allah spoke to Moses with direct speech﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:164]. He alluded to this in Surah Ibrahim in His saying: ﴿Has there not come to you the news of those before you: the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Thamud, and those after them, whom none knows but Allah? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾ [Ibrahim 14:9], and so on. In Surah al-Furqan in His saying: ﴿And 'Ad and Thamud and the companions of the Rass, and many generations between them﴾ [Al-Furqan 25:38], and other verses besides these.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then when the command of Allah comes, it will be judged with truth, and the falsifiers will lose there.﴾ His saying here, "when the command of Allah comes," means the Resurrection (al-Qiyamah, the Day of Standing) has come, as we have previously explained in His saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [An-Nahl 16:1]. That is: when the Resurrection stands, He will judge between people with the truth, which admits no injustice or oppression, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the earth shines with the light of its Lord, and the Book is placed, and the prophets and the witnesses are brought, and judgment is given between them with truth﴾ [Az-Zumar 39:69], to the end of the verse.

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praise of their Lord, and judgment is given between them with truth﴾ [Az-Zumar 39:75].

The truth mentioned in these verses is what is meant by the justice (al-qist) mentioned in Surah Yunus in His saying: ﴿And for every nation there is a messenger; when their messenger comes, judgment is given between them with justice﴾ [Yunus 10:47].

What this noble verse contains, namely that when the Resurrection stands the falsifiers will lose, He, majestic and exalted is He, clarified in Surah al-Jathiyah in His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and on the Day the Hour stands, on that day the falsifiers will lose﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 45:27].

The "mubtil" (falsifier) is one who dies persisting in falsehood.

The loss of the falsifiers mentioned here we have already explained in Surah Yunus, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have indeed lost, and they were not guided﴾ [Yunus 10:45].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the cattle, that you may ride some of them and eat of some of them﴾ ﴿And for you in them are benefits, and that you may reach through them a need in your breasts, and upon them and upon the ships you are carried.﴾ (p-396) We have already mentioned that the word ja'ala (جَعَلَ, "to make/place") comes in the Arabic language with four meanings, three of which are in the Qur'an:

The first: ja'ala used in the sense of i'tiqad (اعْتَقَدَ, "to believe/consider"). Among its examples is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 19], meaning: they believed them to be females. It is known that this form takes two objects, the subject and the predicate.

The second: ja'ala in the sense of sayyara (صَيَّرَ, "to turn into/render"), as in His saying: ﴿until We made them a harvest, extinguished﴾ [al-Anbiya': 15]. This form also takes two objects, the subject and the predicate.

The third: ja'ala in the sense of khalaqa (خَلَقَ, "to create"), as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light﴾ [al-An'am: 1], meaning: He created the heavens and the earth and created the darknesses and the light.

The apparent meaning is that among this usage is His saying here: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the cattle﴾, meaning: He created for you the cattle. This is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the cattle, He created them for you﴾ [an-Nahl: 5], and His saying: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, cattle, so they are their owners?﴾ up to the verse [Ya-Sin: 71].

The fourth, which is not in the Qur'an: ja'ala in the sense of shara'a (شَرَعَ, "to legislate"), as in the poet's words:

"And when I stand up, my garment weighs me down, so I rise like a drunken, intoxicated drinker."

What Allah, exalted is He, mentions in this noble verse of the favours of these abundant blessings, which He bestowed upon them because of His creating for them the cattle, namely the males and females, of camels, cattle, sheep and goats, as we have already explained in surah Ali 'Imran in our discussion of His saying: ﴿and the cattle and the tillage﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 14]. He has also clarified it in other places, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the cattle, He created them for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat.﴾ ﴿And for you in them is beauty when you bring them home and when you send them out to pasture.﴾ ﴿And they carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with difficulty to yourselves﴾ [an-Nahl: 5-7]. Ad-daff' (الدِّفْءُ, "warmth") is what they warm themselves with in garments made from the hides of cattle and their wool, fur and hair.

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He made for you from your houses a dwelling, and He made for you from the hides of cattle tents which you find light on the day of your travel and the day of your settling, and from their wool, fur and hair furnishings and provision for a time.﴾ [an-Nahl: 80].

• And His saying, exalted is He: (p-397) ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, cattle, so they are their owners?﴾ ﴿And We have subjected them to them, so from them is their riding, and from them they eat.﴾ ﴿And for them in them are benefits and drinks; will they not then be grateful?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71-73].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, for you in the cattle is a lesson: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, from between digestive contents and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers.﴾ [al-Mu'minun/as-Saff: 66 in the source].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, for you in the cattle is a lesson: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, and for you in them are many benefits, and from them you eat.﴾ ﴿And upon them and upon the ships you are carried.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 21-22].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And of the cattle are beasts of burden and those for sprea­ding; eat of what Allah has provided you and do not follow the steps of Satan; indeed, he is to you a manifest enemy.﴾ ﴿Eight mates: of the sheep two and of the goats two﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Or were you witnesses when Allah instructed you with this?﴾ [al-An'am: 142-144].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He sent down for you of the cattle eight mates﴾ [az-Zumar: 6].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He made for you mates from yourselves, and from the cattle mates﴾ up to the verse [ash-Shura: 11].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and the cattle that you ride﴾ up to the verse [az-Zukhruf: 12],

along with other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 82:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾. Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. This is the way of Allah which has passed before among His servants.
